plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: Layered branches carry broad, petal-like bracts that float above the bare woodland understory like a drift of white lace. The small greenish true flowers cluster at the center of each bloom. By mid-spring the whole tree glows against the fresh green of the forest edge.
plants.location: Eastern United States, from the Northeast down to the Southeast
plants.funFact: What look like four large petals are modified leaves called bracts. The real flowers are the tiny yellow-green buttons in the middle, and the tree's bright red fall berries feed many songbirds.

plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: This twining vine drapes pergolas, walls and old trees in long, fragrant chains of lavender-blue flowers. The blooms open almost all at once, usually before the leaves unfurl, so the plant looks like a shimmering purple waterfall. The sweet scent attracts bumblebees and carpenter bees.
plants.location: Native to China and widely grown in gardens across East Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: A mature wisteria can live for well over a century. Its twisting stems are strong enough to crush weak supports, and they twine in a consistent direction, counterclockwise when seen from above.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Cup-shaped blooms in nearly every color stand in neat rows and swaths across the Dutch bulb fields. Mid-April is the peak of the display, when whole fields look like stripes of paint. Cut flowers and garden beds across the temperate Northern Hemisphere join in at the same time.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-March to mid-May, with peak bloom around mid-April
plants.location: Lisse and the bulb-growing region of the Netherlands
plants.funFact: Tulips originated in the mountains of Central Asia. In 17th-century Holland they became so prized that single bulbs sold for the price of a fine house during the famous 'tulip mania'.
